prompt:
Build a closed-loop lane-following system in Simulink that combines synthetic forward radar and monocular-vision detections, multi-object sensor fusion, detected lane geometry, coupled longitudinal/lateral model-predictive control, and a finite-mass vehicle model. The environment must generate moving traffic and lane boundaries for straight-target, stop-and-go, and curved cut-in/cut-out operation. Radar and vision vehicle detections must feed a connected fusion/tracking path that selects the relevant lead vehicle. Vision-derived lane boundaries must feed a connected lane-center estimator. The controller must use the fused lead range and range rate for spacing control and use previewed lane curvature, lateral deviation, and lane-relative yaw for lateral path control. Its acceleration and steering commands must drive the vehicle dynamics, whose updated state must return to the environment and sensors to close the loop.

Read lane_following_input from the MATLAB base workspace. Its traffic_scenario field is straight_target, stop_and_go, or curved_cut_in_out. driver_set_velocity_mps is in 20--31 m/s, time_gap_s is in 1.2--2.4 s, and default_spacing_m is in 8--14 m. Use a controller sample time of 0.1 s. The precise tracker, lane-fit, MPC, and vehicle equations are not prescribed, but the sensing, estimation, control, and vehicle paths must be causal and connected. The system must respond materially when the requested velocity, time gap, or traffic scenario changes; fixed replay, prescribed ego trajectories, disconnected sensors, or direct copying of scenario truth to the published fusion outputs is not valid.

Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named ego_acceleration, ego_velocity, driver_set_velocity, relative_distance, relative_velocity, lateral_deviation, relative_yaw_angle, steering_angle, and collision. Each is a scalar one-channel Timeseries: ego_acceleration is one channel in m/s^2; ego_velocity, driver_set_velocity, and relative_velocity are in m/s; relative_distance and lateral_deviation are in m; relative_yaw_angle and steering_angle are in rad; and collision is a unitless Boolean or 0/1 value. relative_distance and relative_velocity must be the lead-vehicle state delivered by the connected radar/vision fusion and tracking path. lateral_deviation and relative_yaw_angle must come from the connected detected-lane processing path. Acceleration and steering must be the commands that actually drive the vehicle model, and all logs must come from the same causal simulation. The system should avoid collision, keep acceleration and steering within plausible actuator limits, maintain useful spacing and speed regulation, follow curved lanes, and remain stable through stop-and-go and cut-in/cut-out transients. Save the completed model as cand_XAUTO09.slx in the submission directory and keep the latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XAUTO09.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
